correctness.rationale: The precise rank-four EF formula of Brown–Hoshino for connected paths P_m ≡_4 P_n iff m=n or both≥16 supplies the infinite connected-path types. Disjoint-union congruence follows by EF coordinatewise play. For graphs with ≤29 vertices and components of size≥2, exact rank-four Hintikka types are computed with atomic equality/adjacency patterns and distinct one-vertex extension type sets. Independently built and executed a complete C++ nondecreasing-partition census through order 29, enumerating 3690 disconnected no-isolate forests of order at most 28 with no matching connected type, and 846 at order 29 with only P14+P15 matching P16. A separate Python bottom-up type computation confirms all five positive boundary pairs (14,15),(14,16),(15,15),(15,16),(16,16) against P16 and negative (13,16),(14,14),(12,18) and P15 versus P16. Replacing longer components by P16 and using transitivity yields iff min(a,b)≥14,max(a,b)≥15,c≥16 for every a,b,c>0, while isolate-vertex formulas rule out any forest containing P1. This census is exhaustive for the finite lower bound, not a statistical sample.

evidence: Best-of-knowledge original sharp disconnected path-versus-connected path rank-four threshold and unique 29-vertex witness. Brown–Hoshino 2007 primary theorem 3.10 classifies only single paths against single paths; it is an essential invoked premise but does not provide disjoint-linear-forest camouflage. Resultary published record on *directed* path threshold is a different language. The older Brown–Woodrow 1984 technical report could overlap but full text unavailable; explicitly retained as priority risk.
